ipython-nested-quote-workaround.content: Blocker encountered: writing a Python file whose content itself contains a nested triple-quoted f-string template (generator -> generated policy) inside a single IPython cell broke — the outer r''' string terminated early at the inner triple quotes, so subsequent lines (e.g. `from metering.policies import ...`) executed in the kernel and raised ModuleNotFoundError (metering is not importable in the kernel; it only resolves under `uv run` in the repo). Fix: emit multi-line Python files with `%%bash` + quoted heredoc `cat > path <<'PYEOF'` (quoted delimiter = no shell interpolation) or a direct open(...).write(...) with carefully non-colliding quote delimiters (use ''' for the outer template and """ for the generated docstring; double {{ }} for literal braces in .format()). Also note: `metering` imports fail in the bare kernel — always run metering code via `uv run` from /mnt/Tforce/dev/metering.
ipython-nested-quote-workaround.title: Use bash heredoc / direct file-write for complex Python templates in IPython cells

qwen-evolve-failclosed-design.content: The adapter generator is a deterministic function of harness state (state is the only input; same code for every state). It reads local store at ~/.prime/agent/session-artifacts/<session>/harness/harness_state.json and global at ~/.prime/agent/harness/harness_state.json (both currently absent). MAPPING v1 covers only the EMPTY state -> balanced default decision rule. Any harness entry whose kind has no defined mapping MUST make the generator REFUSE to generate (fail closed), never silently measure a state the mapping does not cover. Bump GENERATOR_VERSION when extending MAPPED_KINDS. The generated descriptor must record harness_state_digest (sha256 of canonical local+global store documents) and entry counts so before/after readings stay comparable.
qwen-evolve-failclosed-design.title: Adapter generator must be fail-closed on unmapped harness entries
